first_installment_sketch: The authorization rule beat: what we harvested was the mechanism, what we rejected was the framework. The model-proposes, deterministic-kernel-authorizes rule: the LLM proposes an effect and the deterministic kernel decides whether it is authorized, so no model output ever approves its own side effect. That mechanism was mapped onto the existing Capability and Approval authorities instead of being imported with a framework's own truth model. The boundary: external machinery executes, PING decides truth.
hook: We took the mechanism and left the framework.
thesis: MECHANISMS, NOT FRAMEWORKS is a recurring franchise: what we harvested, what we rejected, and the boundary. Each installment names one concrete mechanism harvested from an external system, the authority boundary it respects inside PING, and what was rejected and why. The rule is fixed: the installment names a real mechanism or it does not ship.
title: MECHANISMS NOT FRAMEWORKS
